title: Apple Silicon MLX Backend
description: Soup MLX backend for native LLM fine-tuning on Apple Silicon M1–M4 without CUDA: SFT, and since v0.77.0 DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO through Soup's own MLX loop.

blocks.html:
Apple Silicon MLX Backend

Soup v0.25.0 added a native MLX training backend for M1 to M4 Macs, running on unified memory without CUDA, Rosetta, or x86 emulation. Since v0.77.0 it trains five tasks: supervised fine-tuning through mlx-lm's tuner, and DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO through Soup's own MLX loop. Every other task, GRPO and the unified task: preference included, is refused at config load. See the table below.

Install

This pulls mlx>=0.20 and mlx-lm>=0.31.3 as optional dependencies. The mlx-lm floor was raised in v0.73.1, to the version the MLX supervised path is actually built against.

Enable the backend

Set backend: mlx in soup.yaml. It is a config key only: soup train has no --backend flag (--backend belongs to soup serve). A minimal config:

blocks.code:
base: mlx-community/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit
backend: mlx
task: sft

data:
  train: data.jsonl
  format: chatml

training:
  epochs: 3
  lr: 1e-4
  batch_size: 2
  lora:
    r: 16
    alpha: 32

blocks.html:
For a preference task on the same backend, see Preference training on MLX below.

Supported tasks

TaskMLXNotes
sft✓mlx-lm's tuner. LoRA, QLoRA on pre-quantized mlx-community 4-bit models, and native DoRA since v0.77.0
dpo✓Since v0.77.0. Soup's own MLX loop, TRL's sigmoid loss with training.dpo_beta; reference log-probs precomputed once from the base, so no second model is loaded
orpo✓Since v0.77.0. TRL 0.29.1's ORPO objective with training.orpo_beta; no reference model
simpo✓Since v0.77.0. TRL 0.29.1's CPO simpo loss, beta fixed at 0.1 as on the transformers backend, with simpo_gamma and cpo_alpha; no reference model
kto✓Since v0.77.0. TRL 0.29.1's KTO objective with training.kto_beta; reference precomputed once from the base; batch_size 2 or more, as on every backend
preference–Refused at config load (tracked as #2202). With preference_loss dpo, orpo or simpo the message names the native task to use
grpo, ppo, ipo, bco, online_dpo, reward_model, embedding, pretrain and the rest–Refused at config load, with an error naming the task. Use backend: transformers

Through v0.76.1 the backend ran sft and nothing else: every other task, DPO included, was refused at config load because mlx-lm ships no training helper for them.

Preference training on MLX

v0.77.0 trains task: dpo, orpo, simpo and kto on backend: mlx through Soup's own loop, on the objectives Soup's transformers backend runs through TRL (#1846, #2073, #2097, #2111, by @dryn85-max; KTO was requested by @Amix29).

blocks.code:
base: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-4bit
task: dpo
backend: mlx

data:
  train: ./prefs.jsonl
  format: dpo
  max_length: 1024

training:
  lr: 2e-5
  dpo_beta: 0.1
  batch_size: 2
  gradient_accumulation_steps: 4
  gradient_checkpointing: true
  seed: 42
  lora:
    r: 16
    alpha: 32

blocks.html:
orpo and simpo take the same format: dpo rows. kto takes format: kto rows and needs batch_size: 2 or more.

  • The same rows as the transformers backend. Rows go through the loader's own format: dpo and format: kto converters and are tokenized the way TRL 0.29 does, so a row that fits in data.max_length trains on the same tokens on either backend. On DPO a pair whose chosen equals its rejected, and a row the chat template cannot slice, are skipped with a count; fewer pairs than training.batch_size after skipping is refused. ORPO and SimPO keep ties, as TRL does. Per-row tools and chat_template_kwargs are not applied.
  • No second model. LoRA B starts at zero, so before the first update the policy is the base model. DPO and KTO compute their reference log-probs from it once, before training, and before a --resume checkpoint loads, so the reference is always the base.
  • LoRA dropout stays on (lora.dropout, default 0.05). TRL turns dropout off on the transformers backend, so set lora.dropout: 0 to match it.
  • Long pairs. The vocabulary head runs in checkpointed chunks, so a batch's full-vocabulary logits are never held at once, and the chunked path is checked against the full model on the first batch. For long pairs set training.gradient_checkpointing: true.
  • A diverged DPO run reports NaN rather than stopping. ORPO, SimPO and KTO stop on a non-finite loss. Upstream's docs call DPO more sensitive to the learning rate than SFT and recommend starting at 2e-5 or below.
  • KTO builds its KL rows the way TRL does and runs batches in dataset order, so training.seed does not reorder its rows: shuffle the file to mix labels.
  • Evaluation runs once per epoch and after the last update. training.eval_steps is refused on these four tasks.
  • Progress. The live panel, the soup ui stream and the tracker show loss and validation loss. The per-objective metrics (reward accuracy and margin, and their equivalents for ORPO and KTO) print on each logged step only when there is no live panel, and are returned in the run result.
  • Resume. ORPO, SimPO and KTO refuse a --resume checkpoint that has no adapter_config.json beside it, or that names another task or another base, before any tensor loads.
  • Output: adapters.safetensors and an adapter_config.json recording the task, its beta and the base, loadable with mlx_lm.load(base, adapter_path=output).

Upstream qualified ORPO, SimPO and KTO on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct in bf16 and 4-bit on an M4 Pro, and says of its own runs that they show the objective moving, not alignment quality. No throughput or memory figure is published here for any MLX preference task.

Refused at load on MLX

Each refusal names the field and what to change. soup doctor --config reports the first cross-field refusal it hits, so fix that setting and run it again until it prints no error.

  • On every MLX task: lora.r: 0 (MLX trains LoRA adapters only), lora.use_vera and a non-random init_strategy, loraplus_lr_ratio (the MLX optimizer uses one learning rate for every LoRA tensor), use_lorafa, relora_steps, rope_scaling_type, freeze_layers / freeze_ratio, data.add_new_tokens / new_special_tokens, stream_layers, multipack, the Quant Menu formats (hqq:* and the rest), loss_spike_recovery and grad_accum_auto_tune. Most of these have been refused since v0.76.0.
  • New in v0.77.0: lora.rank_pattern and alpha_pattern (#1996; the MLX trainer builds every adapter from one scalar rank and alpha, so through v0.76.1 a pattern trained a uniform adapter without a word; an empty {} still loads; upstream calls the refusal a stop-gap until the trainer applies them), data.chat_template (#2051; MLX renders the model's shipped template only), and training.use_mod: true (#1752).
  • On DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO: a non-text modality, DoRA, training.eval_steps, loss_watchdog, dpo_beta_schedule / dpo_ref_regen_epochs, and, on ORPO, SimPO and KTO, quantization: 8bit (use none, or a pre-quantized mlx-community 4-bit base with quantization: 4bit). A preference_loss_weights blend needs task: preference, which MLX refuses.
  • Now accepted on MLX SFT, since v0.77.0: lora.use_dora (text, quantization none or 4bit), training.eval_steps, and training.loss_watchdog (text only).
  • Settings that are only ignored still load and are listed by soup doctor --config (see below).

A few limits are checked only when the trainer starts, so soup doctor --config cannot see them: a training split smaller than batch_size on MLX SFT is refused before the model loads, as is eval_steps with an empty validation split; DPO, ORPO and SimPO refuse fewer pairs than batch_size after skipping, and KTO fewer than two rows.

DoRA on MLX

training.lora.use_dora: true on text SFT uses mlx-lm's native weight-decomposed adapter (v0.77.0, #1920, by @Amix29). It supports dense linear targets on an unquantized or pre-quantized 4-bit base, with the same scalar lora.r, lora.alpha and target_modules as MLX LoRA. Switch or expert layers, embedding targets, unmatched target names and 8-bit layers are refused before the adapter is converted. use_rslora, rank_pattern, alpha_pattern and quantization: 8bit are refused at load. The output records fine_tune_type: dora and loads with mlx_lm.load(base, adapter_path=output). A warm start refuses missing, extra or differently shaped tensors, magnitudes included. Upstream's tests use a tiny random model: they establish the adapter lifecycle, not quality or a speed advantage over LoRA.

rsLoRA on MLX

lora.use_rslora: true is applied on MLX since v0.77.0 (#1899, by @ndablizov): the scale alpha / sqrt(r) goes into adapter_config.json and into training. Through v0.76.1 it loaded and was never read, so such runs trained at the plain-LoRA scale alpha / r, an 8x smaller update at the default r: 64, alpha: 16. The same config now trains at the rsLoRA scale, so its results change; drop the flag to keep the old scale. MLX DoRA refuses it.

Evaluation and small splits

  • training.eval_steps: N on MLX SFT (v0.77.0, #2074) evaluates after every N completed optimizer updates (after accumulation) and once after the last. Every validation row counts, including a tail smaller than one batch, weighted by supervised tokens. The interval is recorded in adapter_config.json, and an empty validation split is refused before the model loads. Unset, mlx-lm keeps its own cadence.
  • A validation split smaller than one batch (the default val_split: 0.1 gives one row on a 10-row file) is not evaluated when eval_steps is unset. The run warns, naming both numbers, and records no val_loss; set data.val_split: 0 to train on those rows instead, or set eval_steps, which evaluates such a split. Through v0.76.1 that split crashed the run at its first evaluation, after the model had loaded (#1857).
  • A training split smaller than one batch is refused before the model loads.

The loss watchdog on MLX SFT

training.loss_watchdog: true works on MLX text SFT since v0.77.0 (#2115, by @Amix29), with the usual loss_watchdog_threshold and loss_watchdog_patience. Reports count completed optimizer updates (every logging_steps updates). A triggering report stops training at a completed optimizer update and saves the current adapter, and adapter_config.json records the stop reason and the work actually completed. It saves the last state, not a best-loss checkpoint. The other MLX tasks and modalities refuse the watchdog, and MLX still refuses loss_spike_recovery.

Diagnostics

On Apple Silicon this reports Backend: MPS (Apple Silicon) and whether it is available, and since v0.76.0 it also prints an MLX panel with the installed MLX version, the chip name and the unified memory; if MLX is not installed the panel says not installed and prints pip install "soup-cli[mlx]". (Through v0.75.2 soup doctor never reported MLX: the helper that would fill those in had no caller, so the version always read unknown. This was written from the code at the tag and not run on an Apple machine.) It does not report a recommended batch size. soup doctor --config soup.yaml is the part of this command that knows what the MLX backend does not read, and it is documented below.

Since v0.73.3, device detection knows this backend exists. Before that, detect_device() only probed PyTorch MPS and fell back to cpu, so an MLX run announced "CPU (no GPU detected)" — and the label was never the harm. That fallback also fired a "4bit quantization is not supported on CPU" warning and silently rewrote quantization: 4bit to none, on every MLX run that asked for 4-bit. With backend: mlx set, detection now resolves to MLX with the chip name, reports Apple unified memory in telemetry, and preserves 4bit for pre-quantized mlx-community checkpoints, which is a different thing from bitsandbytes NF4 and was never what that warning was written about. The CUDA-shaped analytical VRAM pre-flight is also skipped on this path, because Apple unified memory is managed by Metal rather than by a fixed VRAM pool.

Also since v0.73.3: [mlx] is a self-contained install for SFT on local JSONL, JSON or CSV data, and since v0.77.0 for DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO too, so you never need the PyTorch stack just to train on a Mac. Since v0.74.0 you may combine them: pip install "soup-cli[train,mlx]" resolves, because both extras now declare the same transformers>=5.16.1,<6.0.0 floor. Before that release the two declared ranges that could not be satisfied together at all, so the combination was not a style preference but an outright resolver failure. [train] is still the PyTorch and TRL stack the Transformers backend uses. A Hugging Face Hub or streaming dataset still needs datasets, because that data source owns the dependency; a local file path does not.

MLX-native recipes

  • llama3.1-8b-sft-mlx — M2+ 16GB. Its model, mlx-community/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-4bit, was also trained on an 8 GB M1 under a smaller config than the recipe's (LoRA r=8, batch 1, max_length: 512, 48 rows, one epoch): 48 iterations in 71 s at a 5.154 GB peak, adapter written and reloadable. The recipe's own settings (r=16, batch 2, max_length: 2048, 3 epochs) were not run on that machine
  • qwen3-8b-sft-mlx — M2+ 16GB. Its repo ID was broken until v0.75.0, pointing at mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-Instruct-4bit, which does not exist; it now names mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit
  • gemma3-4b-sft-mlx — M1+ 16GB. Renamed in v0.75.0, from gemma3-9b-sft-mlx: there is no 9B Gemma 3, so the old name pointed at a repository that raised RepositoryNotFoundError. It now names mlx-community/gemma-3-4b-it-4bit

Use any of them with soup recipes use <name>. The old gemma3-9b-sft-mlx name exits 1.

qwen3-8b-sft-mlx behaves differently after v0.75.0, and the change is a refusal rather than a regression. It does not set data.train_on_responses_only, so it takes the true default, which reached nothing on this backend until now. Qwen3's chat template injects its thinking block only for the last assistant turn, which means partial renderings are not prefixes of the full one and MLX cannot build a per-token mask it can vouch for. Single-turn and system-plus-single-turn rows train as before; multi-turn rows are now refused at dataset construction, before the training loop starts, with a message naming data.train_on_responses_only: false as the remedy. Set that to restore the old behaviour on multi-turn Qwen3 data, knowing it trains on the prompt. llama3.1-8b-sft-mlx and gemma3-4b-sft-mlx mask correctly on both shapes and are unaffected.

The six options this backend accepted and never read

v0.75.0 is the release named for this page. Training options were validated by the schema, documented in these pages, accepted by the config loader, and then read by nothing on backend: mlx. Upstream's release notes count six; the table below lists every setting its fix entries name, eight in all. The same soup.yaml trained a different recipe on Apple Silicon than it did on a CUDA box, silently, and nothing warned.

OptionWhat actually happened before v0.75.0
data.train_on_responses_onlyDefaults to true and reached nothing, so every MLX run trained on system and user turns, and the adapter metadata recorded mask_prompt: false regardless
training.optimizerEvery run built a bare AdamW. All 32 allowlisted names became AdamW (the allowlist is 24 names since v0.76.0)
training.schedulerNo schedule at all: a constant learning rate, whatever the recipe said
training.warmup_ratioIgnored, for the same reason
training.weight_decayIgnored
training.max_grad_normIgnored. The documented default clips every transformers run at 1.0; on MLX nothing clipped anywhere, and the MLX backend ignores: advisory did not even mention it
training.gradient_accumulation_stepsmlx-lm's own dataclass default of 1 always applied, so the effective batch size and the optimizer-update cadence were not the ones you configured. adapter_config.json also hardcoded 1, so the drift was not detectable from the output afterwards
training.gradient_checkpointingmlx-lm's default of False always applied, giving up the memory saving you enabled it for. adapter_config.json hardcoded false here too

All of them are honoured now, and three of the consequences are worth stating with their measurements rather than in the abstract.

Response-only masking is not comparable between the two backends, and MLX is the stricter one. Setting mlx-lm's own flag was not the fix: it masks a single prefix ending before the last message, so on multi-turn chat it supervises only the final assistant turn. Measured on Apple Silicon over 16 two-turn conversations: 772 supervised tokens unmasked, 71 with upstream's flag, 146 with a correct mask. Soup injects its own per-token mask for chat rows, uses upstream's flag for prompt-and-completion rows where it is correct, and warns on plain-text rows because upstream raises there. MLX excludes the assistant header from the loss where the transformers path includes it, and MLX refuses a chat template whose partial renderings are not prefixes of the full one rather than approximating. data.train_on_messages_with_train_field and data.train_on_prompt have no MLX equivalent and now appear in the MLX backend ignores: line instead of vanishing.

max_grad_norm rescues a specific failure, not every run. One M1 step on a deliberately ill-conditioned batch moved SGD weights by 388.03 unclipped against 0.0085 at max_grad_norm: 1.0. AdamW moved 0.126505 against 0.126504, because Adam normalises by its second moment anyway. So this matters for optimizer: sgd and for gradient spikes, and barely registers on an Adam-family run. The norm that actually ran is recorded in adapter_config.json.

Upgrade note, and it applies to anyone who never touched the field. gradient_accumulation_steps defaults to 4. An MLX run that used to update the optimizer on every micro-batch now accumulates over four first: a 4x larger effective batch size and roughly a quarter as many optimizer updates for the same iters. That is the schema default finally taking effect, so a differently-converging run after upgrading is expected rather than a regression. iters is also rounded down to a whole number of accumulation groups, with a floor of one group, because mlx-lm only updates on it % accum == 0 and never flushes a trailing partial group: without that, a dataset smaller than the accumulation window trained for zero optimizer updates.

Optimizers and schedules

Soup's optimizer allowlist is far wider than anything MLX ships, so most valid values have no equivalent here. Since v0.75.0 a value MLX cannot express is refused by name when the optimizer is built, rather than silently becoming AdamW.

SettingAccepted on MLX
training.optimizeradamw_torch, adamw_hf, adamw_torch_fused, sgd, adafactor, adagrad, rmsprop, muon — eight of the 24 on Soup's allowlist. adamw_hf and muon are the two names that work only on this backend: they are refused at config load on transformers and unsloth (v0.76.0)
training.schedulercosine, linear, constant, constant_with_warmup
training.weight_decayAny value, except that a non-zero decay on adagrad or rmsprop is refused, because those MLX constructors take no weight_decay at all and dropping it silently is the bug this module exists to fix

Run a recipe that needs anything else on backend: transformers.

The schedule is built in optimizer-update units, not iterations, because that is what MLX drives a callable learning rate from. Your real warmup is warmup_ratio x (iters // gradient_accumulation_steps); building it against iterations would stretch the warmup by the accumulation factor and never reach the cosine floor. Measured on Apple Silicon, a cosine run with warmup_ratio: 0.2 now reports 10 distinct learning rates across 40 iterations where the old path reported one. A warmup_ratio that rounds to zero updates says so.

The effective plan is written into adapter_config.json — optimizer, scheduler, warmup_updates, total_updates, weight_decay, peak_lr — so what ran is recoverable from the output directory rather than inferred from the recipe.

This backend now drives the dashboard, the tracker and the stream

MLXSFTTrainerWrapper.train() accepted display, tracker and run_id and discarded them, so an MLX run showed mlx-lm's raw stdout while the same config on the transformers path got the Rich panel. Since v0.75.0 it drives all three: the live terminal dashboard, the soup ui SSE stream and the SQLite experiment tracker.

It is an adapter rather than a reuse of the transformers callback, and the reason is worth knowing: mlx-lm exposes only on_train_loss_report and on_val_loss_report, so bridging through a Hugging Face TrainerCallback would have meant faking trainer state. Two deliberate consequences: speed carries iterations_per_second to match the transformers path, because the panel hard-labels that field it/s; and grad_norm is left unset, because mlx-lm does not compute one and a field reading a plausible 0.0 on one backend is worse than an absent one. Verified against real mlx-lm on an 8 GB M1.

The native DPO, ORPO, SimPO and KTO loops (v0.77.0) drive the same three: loss and validation loss on the panel, the tracker and the stream. Their per-objective metrics are not on the panel (see Preference training on MLX), and they evaluate once per epoch and after the last update.

Validation loss is recorded at all for the first time, and MLX produces it too (unset, mlx-lm evaluates the validation split on its own cadence; since v0.77.0 training.eval_steps sets it on SFT, see Evaluation and small splits). Before v0.75.0 the callback read the training loss and never the evaluation loss, so an evaluation step left the last training loss in place and re-reported it: the evaluated number existed nowhere. (Since closed in v0.76.0 for the transformers backend: it never scheduled an evaluation at all until then, so its held-out split was withheld from training and unused; see Training methods.) The live panel gains a Val loss row, and the metrics table and the SSE frame each carry val_loss as its own series, never folded into loss. The panel carries the last measured value forward between evaluations; the stored and streamed values do not, so a step where no evaluation ran records NULL and a series read back has one point per measurement rather than one per logged step. Existing ~/.soup/experiments.db files are migrated in place, and rows written before this ship read NULL rather than a fabricated 0.0, because an unmeasured value must not read as a measured one.

soup doctor --config: the settings your backend does not read

A field can be declared, validated and documented and still be read by nothing on the backend you chose. That is what this whole page is about, and v0.75.0 added the command that tells you before the run instead of during it.

It loads the config, prints Config check - task=<t> backend=<b>, and then either lists the settings your config switches on that the backend does not read, with the reason and the issue that recorded it, or says None of the N setting(s) known to be unread on task=<t> backend=<b> is switched on in this config. Only fields you actually set to an on value are listed, never the ones sitting at a schema default, written at their schema default, or written in their off position (loss_watchdog: false is not reported): a wall of hundreds of rows is not a pre-flight check.

The scope is deliberately narrow, and that is the honest framing. At v0.77.0 the table has eight declared (task, backend, modality) entries: sft on mlx with 12 settings, all reported as ignored (use_galore, use_lorafa, use_ring_attention, use_flash_attn, data.train_on_messages_with_train_field, data.mask_history, data.train_on_prompt, use_liger, neftune_alpha, moe_lora, quantization_aware, use_fsdp2_compile); dpo, orpo, simpo and kto on mlx with 9 each (the SFT list less its three masking switches); sft on unsloth with none left (its precision settings are refused at load); and sft on transformers with vision or audio data, with one each (data.mask_history). At v0.76.x it was four entries, with 18 settings on MLX SFT (seed, data_seed and use_mod among them, and three marked rejected); it was seven entries on one pair through v0.75.2. Some rows can never print, because the loader refuses the setting first: use_lorafa and quantization_aware on every MLX task, and use_liger and use_flash_attn on the four preference tasks. Such a config gets Config could not be loaded (see above). and exit 2 instead. A config setting use_galore, data.mask_history, use_liger, neftune_alpha and moe_lora on MLX SFT prints a five-row table. Every other task-and-backend pair has no table, so for those the command prints the None of the N setting(s)... line, which there means "not reviewed" and never "checked and fine" (a DPO config on the transformers backend setting use_ring_attention: true, which no trainer applies, gets that line). Upstream tracks that gap itself (#1815). Backend support is declared by hand rather than inferred, because inference does not work: reachability over the import graph detected none of five independently-known MLX gaps, reading the trainer module alone invents gaps for fields that live in helper modules, and --dry-run exits before a trainer is ever constructed. A guard keeps the table honest in both directions, so an entry marked unread fails the suite once any declared module reads the field.

soup doctor --config exits 2 when the config cannot be read, parsed or validated — all three deliberately agree, so this leg can gate CI — and soup doctor exits 1 when a required core dependency is missing or out of range, while the optional [train] group stays advisory.

Two disclosures upstream publishes with it, and they belong here. Five entries were removed from that table before merge, because the same release wired those fields — the guard is what noticed. And the all-clear message overclaimed: the field-consumer guard behind it catches a field nothing reads, not a field something reads wrongly, and a CUDA-only kernel setting that nobody declared is absent from the table. use_liger was the example through v0.75.2, when the message read "Every setting this config writes is read on this backend"; since v0.76.0 use_liger is one of the ignored entries (one of the 12 on MLX SFT at v0.77.0) and the message is the narrower None of the N setting(s)... line. Read that line as "nothing in the declared table is switched on", which is a narrower statement than "every setting is read".

Limitations

  • Single-device only, no distributed MLX training.
  • Base models must be MLX-format (typically from the mlx-community HF org).
  • bitsandbytes is unused on this backend: quantization comes from the MLX model itself.
  • Unsloth backend is not MLX-compatible (they're separate execution paths).
  • Apple Silicon streaming and MPS training are experimental. v0.74.0 turned on BF16 autocast for hardware-validated resident supervised, DPO, reward-model, PRM and GRPO training on capable MPS runtimes behind a live capability probe, with the process-reward path deliberately keeping fp32 master weights to avoid a fatal Metal optimizer dtype mismatch, and unvalidated MPS and CPU staying fp32. Layer streaming keeps its host store genuinely on the CPU there, refusing any allocation that is not real CPU memory, and preserves a BF16 checkpoint instead of silently doubling the store and disk cache to FP32. No claim is made that streaming fits a larger model or runs faster than resident MPS training, and backend: mlx is still rejected with stream_layers because they are separate model-loading paths.
  • On the transformers backend on Apple Silicon MPS (not backend: mlx), soup train, soup sweep and soup bench train set HF_DEACTIVATE_ASYNC_LOAD=1 since v0.77.0 unless you exported a value, because transformers' threaded weight loader crashed soup train with SIGABRT on some setups (#2076, #2040). soup doctor shows the value in its MPS panel. An MLX run's device is mlx, so nothing is set there.
  • Seeded since v0.77.0 (#1855, by @dryn85-max). On SFT, training.seed seeds MLX's own RNG (mx.random, which draws LoRA A and dropout) before the adapter is built, and numpy's global RNG, which mlx-lm's batch shuffle draws from, is seeded with training.data_seed (or training.seed when that is unset) right before training. DPO, ORPO and SimPO seed mx.random and their batch order the same way; KTO runs in dataset order, as TRL's KTO does. An unset seed resolves to 42. Upstream's check is that two runs with the same seed reproduce each other's losses. Through v0.76.1 MLX seeded neither RNG and only warned MLX backend ignores: training.seed, so every run trained on a different batch order, and a run started before v0.77.0 cannot be reproduced. See seeds and reproducibility.
  • The settings refused at config load are listed under Refused at load on MLX above. The ones in the doctor --config table that are only ignored (use_flash_attn on SFT, moe_lora, neftune_alpha and so on) still load: the MLX trainers print MLX backend ignores: training.neftune_alpha, for example, and soup doctor --config lists it.

If you resumed an MLX run before v0.74.0, it started from scratch

--resume auto and a direct --resume <path> only recognised checkpoint-N directories, which is the shape the transformers and Unsloth paths write. mlx-lm's tuner saves step-numbered NNNNNNN_adapters.safetensors files instead, so an MLX run's own output never matched, and training silently restarted from zero every time.

The located checkpoint's adapter weights are loaded before training starts now, and what that is, is stated plainly: a weights-only warm start, not a full resume. mlx-lm's LoRA trainer exposes no optimizer state and no step count, so the step counter and the data position both restart at zero however far the checkpoint got, and the run says so rather than implying otherwise. The same fix also covers a config with experiment_name set, which the first attempt missed.

The same holds for the native preference tasks (v0.77.0). ORPO, SimPO and KTO refuse a checkpoint that has no adapter_config.json beside it, or that names another task or another base, before any tensor loads. DPO and KTO compute their reference log-probs from the base model before the checkpoint's weights load, so the reference is always the base. A DoRA warm start refuses missing, extra or differently shaped tensors, magnitudes included.

If you set use_rslora or a rank pattern on MLX before v0.77.0

Both settings loaded on backend: mlx through v0.76.1 and were never applied, so the run finished and the adapter was not the one the config asked for.

If youWhat happenedWhat to do
Set lora.use_rslora: trueThe run trained plain-LoRA scaling, alpha / r: an 8x smaller update than asked at the default r: 64, alpha: 16 (#1899)Re-run if you wanted rsLoRA. On v0.77.0 the same config trains at alpha / sqrt(r) and its results change; drop the flag to keep the old scale
Set lora.rank_pattern or lora.alpha_patternThe config loaded, passed soup train --dry-run and trained a uniform adapter from the scalar lora.r and lora.alpha; soup doctor --config listed nothing (#1996)v0.77.0 refuses the keys on MLX. Deleting them changes nothing about what trains; if the per-module ranks mattered, train on backend: transformers, which applies them

Known limitation, open through v0.75.2 and since closed in v0.76.0: soup doctor never reported MLX. The MLX version always read unknown, because _get_mlx_info() was defined in the doctor command and called from nowhere. soup doctor now prints the MLX panel described under Diagnostics. soup doctor --config soup.yaml was never affected: that leg reads the config rather than the runtime.

If you trained on this backend before v0.73.1, re-run it

Two defects meant an MLX run could complete successfully and be worthless, and both are repaired in v0.73.1.

  • backend: mlx never dispatched to the MLX trainer at all. It fell through silently to the transformers path. And without a freeze first, what it saved was not an adapter but a full fine-tune: 172 tensors where 24 were expected on a 1.2B model.
  • The MLX adapter_config.json saved target_modules unresolved, as {"keys": ["auto"]}. Loading that file dropped every LoRA tensor without a word, so generation with the adapter was bit-identical to the base model. Since auto is the schema default, this was every MLX run that did not name its modules by hand. The file cannot be repaired after the fact; the run has to be redone.
